data.gender_notes: Pantu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Pantha' meaning vessel, container or carrier. It is also associated with the elephant, a symbol of strength, power and good fortune in Hindu culture. The name Pantu carries the meaning “Vessel, Container” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Pantu usually hope their child will grow to embody vessel, container and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Pantu belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Vessel, Container.”

data.cultural_impact: In some regional cultures, the name "Pantu" can refer to a small clay vessel used to transport water or other essential items. In Hinduism, elephants are considered divine and powerful beings. The name "Pantu" might evoke the image of a sturdy, elephant-headed god like Ganesha, who is the remover of obstacles and the patron of arts and sciences. Given this, "Pantu" may carry an association of strength, power, wisdom, and good fortune.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, "Pantu" is a name that symbolizes the divine container or carrier inside an individual. It highlights the idea that each person is both a vessel of the divine (Sarvam Khalvidam Brahman) and a carrier of spiritual essence. "Pantu" may emphasize the spiritual journey of carrying one's dharma (duty or life purpose) in the service of the whole and serving as a vessel for others in their spiritual growth. It underscores the role of grace and devotion in one's life, acknowledging the presence of the divine in the deepest aspects of existence.

historical_references.reference:
Pantu was a legendary king of the Panchala kingdom mentioned in the Mahabharata, an Indian epic.
Time period: Circa 3000 BCE
Context: Pantu was the father of Draupadi, the common wife of the five Pandava brothers.

Pantu Rai was a king of the Chand dynasty, ruling the region of Tanahun in Nepal from 1443 to 1482 CE
Time period: Late Middle Ages
Context: Pantu Rai is remembered for his successful military campaigns against various invading forces, including the Mughals.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Pantu continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
